get.description: The process is up. Used by container liveness probes.
The app can serve traffic, which means the database is reachable.
Which sign-in methods the login screen should offer.

post.description: Exchange the refresh cookie for a new access token; the refresh token rotates.
Change your password. Other sessions are signed out; this one stays signed in.

get.description: Start sign-in: redirect the browser to Microsoft.
Microsoft redirects here with an authorization code (or an error).
Active users a lead can be assigned to. Open to every signed-in user.

Filter by source, category, priority, status, owner (`me`, `unassigned` or a user
id), score range and free text; sort by newest, score or latest activity.

patch.description: Change status and/or owner. Moving a lead out of `new` counts as its first response.

get.description: Nearest past leads by meaning (pgvector), most similar first.

post.description:
Queue a reply on the lead's channel (email threaded, or WhatsApp within 24 hours).
It is sent by the worker; follow `delivery_status` on the returned message.
Check the inbox now instead of waiting for the next minute.

get.description: Newest first; page with `before` (the `created_at` of the last item).

Server-Sent Events: `ready`, then `notification` for each new one, then `expired`
when the access token runs out. Send the token as a Bearer header (use a fetch-based
client; EventSource can't set headers). On `expired` or a dropped connection, refresh
the token, reconnect and reload the list: events missed while disconnected aren't
replayed.

post.description: Let the app act as the signed-in user. Send the browser to `redirect_url`.

delete.description: Revoke the app's access at once: its tokens stop working on the next call.

get.description:
Leads opened in the last `days` days. Daily volume is bucketed in `timezone` (an IANA
name; defaults to REPORTING_TIMEZONE).
Every settings document, with defaults filled in for ones never saved.

put.description:
Replace one document (e.g. `scoring.weights`). It is validated as a whole, so an
invalid value changes nothing.

post.description:
How the latest scored leads would score with these weights and thresholds. Nothing is
saved.

get.description: Which external services are configured (never their secrets).
Meta's one-time subscription check: echo the challenge if the verify token matches.

post.description:
Verify, store, enqueue, return 200. All parsing happens in the worker, so Meta gets a
fast answer and a parsing bug can't make it retry (or drop) the delivery.
